Combine indicators into a single score by bay segment and year

Source: R/anlz_category.R
anlz_category.Rd

Combine indicators into a single score by bay segment and year

Usage

anlz_category(
  ...,
  bay_segments = c("OTB", "HB", "MTB", "LTB"),
  yr_min = 2000,
  wt = NULL
)

Arguments

...

named data.frames, passed to anlz_indicators - see its documentation for the expected shape

bay_segments

chr vector of bay segments to include, defaults to c('OTB', 'HB', 'MTB', 'LTB'), the four segments with the most complete indicator coverage

yr_min

integer, minimum year to include, defaults to 2000

wt

named numeric vector of weights, keyed by the indicator values produced by anlz_indicators (e.g. c(chla_thresh = 2, fib = 1) to weight an indicator, or c(wq = 2, sed = 1) when combining category scores via anlz_score). Indicators not named in wt - including all of them when wt = NULL - get a weight of 1, so the default is a plain unweighted mean.

Value

A data.frame with columns bay_segment, yr, outcome (0-1, 1 = best), n_indicator (number of indicators averaged for that segment/year), and one additional column per indicator (named from ... or anlz_indicators's indicator column) holding that indicator's own outcome, NA where a segment/year has no data for it

Details

Stacks ... with anlz_indicators, then averages outcome across whatever indicators have data for a given bay segment/year - see n_indicator in the output for how many contributed. This same averaging step produces a category score when ... are raw indicator outputs, and the final bay segment score when ... are the four category scores (see anlz_score) - the two are mechanically identical.

Examples

anlz_category(
  wq_attain = data.frame(bay_segment = 'OTB', yr = 2020, outcome = 0.8),
  fib = data.frame(bay_segment = 'OTB', yr = 2020, outcome = 0.4)
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   bay_segment    yr outcome n_indicator wq_attain   fib
#>   <chr>       <int>   <dbl>       <int>     <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 OTB          2020     0.6           2       0.8   0.4
